title: Financial Services: +25–35% Conversion Rate Across 4 APAC Markets
excerpt: Persona-led paid media for a global asset manager lifted conversion rates 25-35% in regulated markets with compliance built in. Read the case.
rm_desc: Financial services paid media across four APAC markets lifted conversion rates 25-35%. Read the case.
content: This financial services paid media case covers a global asset manager running campaigns across four APAC markets, where compliance constrains both the message and the measurement.
How compliance shaped this financial services paid media plan

Persona-led targeting ran across the four markets with MAS-grade compliance built into creative and targeting from the start rather than retrofitted. Paid search and programmatic operated as one plan against shared segments, and engagement measurement was chosen deliberately where regulation restricts what conversion data can travel.
Why compliance came before creative, not after

Financial services paid media that treats compliance as a review gate at the end of production loses time and options: creative gets rejected late, and the fix is usually a weaker version of the original idea. MAS regulation in Singapore and equivalent rules elsewhere in the region set real limits on claims, disclosures and targeting; building against those limits from the first creative brief meant nothing needed to be re-shot or rewritten after the fact, and the campaign could launch on schedule across all four markets simultaneously.

Conversion rates improved 25–35% and cost per conversion fell 20–30% across the four markets. Paid-search engagement reached 40.8% (3.9× the CTR benchmark), with 5.9% programmatic engagement across 21.8M in-target impressions.

Several of those are engagement measures, chosen because regulated finance restricts what conversion data can travel. We would rather show the honest metric than dress one up, and in this category, financial services paid media that clears compliance and still performs is the actual achievement, not a footnote to apologise for.
What we could not measure, and why

Down-funnel conversion data, actual account openings and funded amounts, sat behind the client's own compliance and data-residency walls and never reached the media platforms. The missing data marks a deliberate regulatory boundary that any honest financial services paid media engagement in this category has to work within. Engagement metrics are the closest proxy available on the media side; the client tracked the down-funnel numbers separately and reconciled them internally, which is the correct division of responsibility in a regulated category.

This engagement ran through our paid media service, with reporting built on the same honest-measurement principles covered on our analytics page. Asset managers and other regulated financial services paid media buyers weighing a similar four-market rollout can use either page as a starting reference.

Regulatory language, permitted claims and disclosure requirements varied market by market even within the same APAC region, so a single creative asset with a single compliance sign-off never worked across all four. Financial services paid media at this scale means budgeting for market-specific legal review as a real line item and a real timeline dependency, not an afterthought squeezed in before launch. Two of the four markets required a longer review cycle than the other two, which shaped the staggered launch schedule rather than a simultaneous one across all four.
What a regulated buyer should ask an agency

Whether they have actually run financial services paid media through a compliance review process before, instead of only claiming familiarity with the category. Ask for a specific example of a creative asset that changed because of a compliance requirement, and what the change was. An agency that has never had a financial services asset rejected or amended by a compliance team probably has not done enough of this work to know where the real constraints sit.
Client described rather than named, and all figures are reported exactly as recorded at the time.
